extraction.name: LongBench
extraction.description: LongBench is the first bilingual, multi-task benchmark for long context understanding, comprising 21 datasets across 6 task categories in both English and Chinese. It contains 4,750 test instances with an average length of 6,711 words (English) and 13,386 characters (Chinese). Tasks cover single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion. All datasets are standardized into a unified format for automatic evaluation of LLMs.
extraction.creator: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li (Tsinghua University, Zhipu.AI, Institute of Automation Chinese Academy of Sciences)
extraction.citeAs: Bai, Y., Lv, X., Zhang, J., Lyu, H., Tang, J., Huang, Z., Du, Z., Liu, X., Zeng, A., Hou, L., Dong, Y., Tang, J., & Li, J. LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding. arXiv:2308.14508v2 [cs.CL].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected through multiple strategies: (1) direct extraction from existing public datasets, (2) processing and adapting existing datasets for long context evaluation, and (3) manual creation and annotation by the authors. 6 datasets are directly extracted from original datasets, 10 are built based on original datasets and processed for long context evaluation, and 5 are created and annotated by the authors. For multi-doc QA, complete Wikipedia passages were used as context, with supporting and distracting passages combined until reaching a maximum length. For synthetic tasks, passages were randomly sampled from Wikipedia and C4 dataset, with summaries generated using GPT-3.5-Turbo.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sources include: NarrativeQA (literature and film), Qasper (NLP papers), Wikipedia (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, PassageCount, PassageRetrieval-en), Baidu Search and Baidu Zhidao (DuReader), U.S. Government Accountability Office and Congressional Research Service reports (GovReport), meeting transcripts (QMSum, VCSUM), news articles (MultiNews, LSHT), web questions (TREC), Wikipedia and web (TriviaQA), dialogue (SAMSum), GitHub repositories (LCC, RepoBench-P), C4 Dataset (PassageRetrieval-zh), and multi-field documents including legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, and academic papers (MultiFieldQA).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For multi-doc QA, supporting passages were included within the context, then distracting passages were added until reaching maximum length, and passages were randomly ordered. For few-shot learning tasks, a random number of examples was selected from a specified range and randomly sampled from the training set to form the context. For synthetic PassageRetrieval tasks, 30 passages were randomly sampled and one was summarized using GPT-3.5-Turbo. For PassageCount, passages were randomly selected, repeated at random, and shuffled. For code completion (RepoBench-P), cross-file code snippets were shuffled and combined with preceding lines of code.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data was extracted from test sets of public datasets to avoid test leakage (except VCSUM due to insufficient test data). Two extraction strategies were used: random sampling (maintaining natural length distribution for LongBench) and uniform sampling based on length (sampling comparable quantities from 0-4k, 4k-8k, and 8k+ ranges for LongBench-E). For TriviaQA few-shot examples, passages with less than 1,000 words were filtered out. All datasets were standardized into a unified format with input I, context C, and answer A. When input length surpasses model's maximum context length, the input is truncated from the middle.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For MultiFieldQA datasets, three Ph.D. students were invited to annotate questions and answers for each article. Annotation guidelines required: (1) questions should be clear with definitive and relatively short answers, (2) distribution of evidence paragraphs should be random throughout the article, (3) questions should have varied types including information-extracting, summarizing, and multi-hop reasoning questions. Annotators ensured answers could be inferred from documents and evidence placement was random to avoid positional biases. Average annotation time was approximately 5 minutes per sample.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cross-validation among annotators shows a 100% accuracy rate of the annotated answers for MultiFieldQA. The authors ensured that answers can be inferred from the documents and that the placement of evidence is fairly random to avoid biases.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 question-answer pair per document for MultiFieldQA (annotated by 3 Ph.D. students with cross-validation)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Ph.D. students with extensive research experience in the field of NLP, serving as expert annotators.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-3.5-Turbo was used to generate summaries for PassageRetrieval synthetic tasks. Automatic metrics used for evaluation include ROUGE-L, F1, Edit Similarity (Levenshtein distance), and Accuracy (classification and exact match).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: LongBench facilitates research on long context understanding for large language models, enabling more rigorous evaluation of LLMs on tasks that require processing long sequences such as books, reports, and codebases. It supports bilingual (English and Chinese) evaluation, contributing to more comprehensive assessment of LLMs' capabilities across languages.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note that models may rely on memorization rather than context understanding for datasets derived from Wikipedia (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue), as these are common training sources for LLMs. The benchmark also notes that performance on LongBench is coupled with models' instruction-following capabilities, not purely long context understanding.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: (1) Automatic evaluation metrics (ROUGE-L, F1) may not accurately reflect response quality and may underestimate performance for models that generate longer responses. (2) Performance on LongBench is coupled with models' instruction-following capabilities, making it difficult to purely assess long context modeling ability. (3) Summarization and code completion tasks may not be sufficiently discriminating due to similarity-based metrics not being sensitive enough to distinguish between strong and weak models.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and benchmarking of large language models on long context understanding tasks. LongBench is designed for zero-shot evaluation (except few-shot learning tasks). LongBench-E is specifically suited for gauging each model's capability across various context lengths. The benchmark covers single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion as evaluation scenarios.
